signals.title: USD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Intervention
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.42, dropping sharply as the JPY outperformance theme dominates G10 flows following suspected Japanese intervention. The pair has broken below its SMA20 (162.53) and SMA50 (161.34) clusters, now testing the 159.00 handle as the USD -1.394% weekly average laggard status accelerates. Despite a 267bp OIS carry advantage for the USD, the intervention headline has forced a massive unwind of the JPY COT lev_net short (-114,030), which was previously at an extreme. The options market confirms this shift with a moderate 1.38 put skew (25d RR), showing institutions are paying for protection against further USD/JPY downside despite the high carry cost. JPY's ESI of +22.0 supports the fundamental backdrop for strength, while the bear steepener regime in US yields (2s10s +44.3bp) fails to support the DXY. Risk: Intervention remains verbal only and the 267bp carry advantage reasserts dominance above 160.00.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning + Vol + ESI Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD is holding at 0.7028, positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.6911-0.7015), yet facing significant internal friction. While COT data shows specs are net long +20,521 (62.8% long), the AUD ESI has plunged to -16.7, indicating a persistent run of data misses that contradicts the bullish positioning. Options markets are pricing in heavy protection with a VRP of +5.5% (IV 11.7% vs HV30 6.2%), suggesting traders are hedging for a volatility spike rather than chasing the spot move higher. The -70bp AONIA-SOFR carry favors AUD, but the extreme vol premium and negative data surprises create an asymmetric risk to the downside if the 0.7000 level is surrendered. Risk: RBA delivers a hawkish surprise at the August 11 meeting, validating the long positioning despite recent data misses.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence + ESI
signals.text: NZD/USD has rallied to 0.5874, now trading above its SMA200 (0.5825) as a high-conviction squeeze play develops. Speculative positioning remains heavily net short (lev_net -31,649, only 12% long) despite the RBNZ's active hiking cycle and an OCR-overnight rate of 2.5%. This positioning is increasingly untenable as the NZD ESI hits +30.6, marking a period of sustained data outperformance that supports the RBNZ's hawkish stance. The pair has cleared the SMA20/50/200 cluster, and the negative real rate of -1.56% (due to 4.06% inflation expectations) is being overlooked by the market in favor of the nominal hiking path. Continued spot strength will likely force a disorderly unwind of the crowded spec short toward 0.5950. Risk: RBNZ signals a pause at the September 2 meeting, providing relief to the spec shorts.

signals.title: EUR/CHF — Retail Sentiment Divergence
signals.text: EUR/CHF is trading at 0.9286, influenced by a stark divergence between retail positioning and institutional flow. Retail sentiment is at an extreme 87% short, fading the recent EUR strength even as the ECB market bias remains tilted toward a hike. This retail extreme contrasts with a positive EUR ESI of +9.3 and a significant +240bp carry advantage for the EUR over the SNB's 0.0% policy rate. While the 25d RR is near neutral (-0.28), the extreme retail short bias suggests a high probability of a 'pain trade' to the upside, where retail capitulation drives a break toward 0.9400. Risk: Sudden risk-off sentiment (VIX > 25) triggers a safe-haven bid for CHF, compressing the carry spread regardless of retail positioning.
